newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria insolvencies seen at new post-war record.
newsitem.headline: Austria insolvencies seen at new post-war record.

text.p: Austrian insolvencies are expected to reach a new post-war high this year, reflecting a slowdown in the country's economy, Austria's credit watchdog said on Thursday.
The agency said it expected the number of company failures to rise to as high as 5,400 this year, up eight percent on last year's 4,994 -- already a post-war record.
"The highest number of insolvencies so far was recorded in 1932 with 5,580," it added.
Economic growth is expected to slow to a mere 0.7 percent this year, from 1.8 percent last year, and to remain at around one percent in 1997.
Analysts have blamed the record number of company failures, accompanied by rising unemployment, as a key factor for the far right's surge in Austria's European Parliament elections last month.
In the first nine months of the year alone, total liabilities of insolvent firms stood at 43.2 billion schillings ($4.1 billion) , compared to a total of 62 billion schillings in 1995.

Construction group Maculan Holding was the year's most spectacular insolvency with 11.1 billion schillings in liabilities. The group's failure was the biggest to hit a listed Austrian company since World War Two.
Maculan's collapse was followed by another construction group, unlisted Hamberger Baugesellschaft, with liabilities of 1.33 billion schillings.
Austria's biggest insolvency was the collapse of cooperative supermarket chain Konsum with debts of 26 billion schillings last year. ($ = 10.60 Austrian Schillings)
